comparator.name: Literary Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: This Dutch-track example has a 120 EC major and 60 EC of profiling space. The major includes 75 EC of required coursework, a 30 EC depth package, a 7.5 EC context elective and a 7.5 EC thesis. The example uses Literature Across Borders and Rhetoric. Students complete The Republic of Letters to prepare for their thesis. The thesis requires 120 earned EC, including at least 22.5 EC at advanced level.
components: Literary History 1: Antiquity and the Middle Ages
Example of the required context elective.
Required preparation for the literary studies thesis.
Includes a coherent 30 EC package, such as a minor, study abroad or a second literary studies depth package.

core: Close reading, literary interpretation, narrative form and the production of meaning
European and global literary history from antiquity through contemporary literature
Literature in social, cultural and political context, including identity and conflict
Literary research methods, academic criticism and independent research
adjacent: Comparative literature across periods, languages, regions and cultural traditions
Transnational, postcolonial, migration and diaspora approaches to literature
Literature, censorship, dissent, contested pasts, bodies and political conflict
Literature in relation to film, digital culture and other media
questions: How do literary form, genre and narrative technique create meaning?
How do literary texts cross borders and shape cultural identities?
How does literature respond to social power, political conflict and cultural change?

routeSelection.basis: The normalized Literary Studies target does not select between the two formal 30-EC depth packages. The current official programme page and 2026-2027 OER list Literature Across Borders before Literature in Conflict, so it is selected by official order before considering UCR fit. Retorica is selected on the same basis as the first published context elective; the 60-EC profiling space remains open.

selection.assessment: The closest plan builds literary interpretation across periods alongside cultural history and methods. The across-borders plan gives more weight to comparative narratives, migration, media and cultural transfer. The conflict plan develops literary and media analysis around identity, empire, power and dissent. The two additional options reflect distinct academic directions in Utrecht’s degree.

alternatives.label: Literary Studies, History and Cultural Analysis
alternatives.labelReason: Study how literature creates meaning through narrative, form and language. Read works from different periods and combine literary theory and close reading with art, history, film and research methods.
alternatives.concept: Study how literature creates meaning through narrative, form and language. Read works from different periods and combine literary theory and close reading with art, history, film and research methods.
progression: Introductory literature, art and film precede advanced interpretation and research. Qualitative methods precedes advanced cultural and historical inquiry.

alternatives.label: Comparative Literature, Media and Transnational Culture
alternatives.labelReason: Explore how stories travel across cultures and media. Study myths, life and travel writing, adaptation and environmental media, with perspectives from world archaeology, African art and cultural history.
alternatives.concept: Explore how stories travel across cultures and media. Study myths, life and travel writing, adaptation and environmental media, with perspectives from world archaeology, African art and cultural history.
alternatives.distinctness: Adds rhetoric, stylistics, world archaeology, philosophy and environmental media to develop questions about circulation, cultural transfer and adaptation.
progression: Literary and film foundations precede adaptation, comparative narrative and advanced interpretation. Rhetoric precedes persuasive communication.

alternatives.label: Literature, Conflict and Cultural Power
alternatives.labelReason: Study how literature and media portray conflict, inequality and resistance. Use close reading, literary theory, myth, memoir and adaptation to examine power and identity, with historical and social context.
alternatives.concept: Study how literature and media portray conflict, inequality and resistance. Use close reading, literary theory, myth, memoir and adaptation to examine power and identity, with historical and social context.
alternatives.distinctness: Uses literature and media to study conflict and cultural power through histories of gender and empire, political institutions, social movements and public debate.
progression: Introductory literature and a comparative reading survey precede myth, memoir, adaptation and advanced theory. History and qualitative methods support advanced work on representation and conflict.

blocks: Both examine early modern culture. UCR focuses on Renaissance art. Utrecht focuses on literature.
Utrecht studies how literature is produced, circulated and valued and prepares students for their thesis. UCR offers related research practice across courses.
Both introduce literary genres, interpretation and close reading.
Great Literary Works includes classical and medieval texts in a broader survey. Utrecht devotes a course to those periods.
Both analyse how style and form create meaning. UCR also studies language use across genres.
Utrecht studies modern and contemporary literary history. UCR studies material media history and technologies.
Both examine mobility, identity and cultural encounters through writing.
Both examine race, identity, representation and power. UCR applies these questions to media.
Both develop critical interpretation of culture. UCR studies theories of literary meaning and reading.
Both examine environmental questions through culture. UCR emphasises visual and audiovisual media.
Utrecht focuses on contemporary debates in literary studies. UCR offers related social and cultural theory.
UCR examines the historical context of modern Europe. Utrecht studies literature from 1789 to 1914.
Both study how arguments and rhetorical choices influence audiences.
Utrecht teaches methods for literary inquiry. UCR develops related skills in qualitative research design and interpretation.
Unmatched comparator components and choice space
Utrecht devotes a course to utopian imagination. UCR addresses related ideas across literature and cultural studies.
Utrecht requires an individual 7.5 EC thesis after preparatory study. UCR offers optional independent research outside the scheduled courses.
Utrecht leaves 60 EC for profiling. At least 30 EC must form a coherent package.

notes.text: Utrecht studies literary history in four periods and requires advanced literary research. The UCR options study literature alongside media, visual culture, history and social science. Utrecht’s required thesis and UCR’s optional independent research have different roles in the degree.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

audience.programmeDescription: Utrecht’s Literary Studies bachelor studies literary history, interpretation and the relationship between literature and society.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The 2026–2027 Dutch-track example follows Literature Across Borders. The UCR options emphasise literary history, cultural transfer, or conflict and cultural power.
